prompt:
Create exactly one file codec.rs with Muse's native write_file tool now.
This is an independent lossless Rust telemetry-compression experiment: byteplanes.
Hypothesis: Investigate column-specific byte-plane or digit-position streams for variable-width numeric lexemes. Store exact token lengths and transpose character positions within each column before zstd; avoid numeric conversion. Account for all lengths/line endings and choose plain transpose if the representation is larger. This is a distinct representation experiment, not a zstd-level sweep.

Fixed parent API (do not redefine):
pub const MAX_INPUT: usize = 2 * 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_PAYLOAD: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
pub const MAX_MODEL: usize = 64 * 1024;
pub type CodecError = String;

pub trait Codec {
    fn train(_samples: &[&[u8]]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError> {
        Ok(Vec::new())
    }
    fn encode(input: &[u8], model: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError>;
    fn decode(encoded: &[u8], model: &[u8], original_len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError>;
}

Use crate::{Codec, CodecError}, export pub struct Candidate, implement Codec.
Safe helpers: crate::toolkit::zstd_compress(input, level) and
crate::toolkit::zstd_decompress(encoded), both Result<Vec<u8>, String>.
Use zstd level 19 for these experiments so backend effort matches the strong
reference. Encoder time is allowed up to 30 seconds per <=2 MiB block; only
decode throughput is a speed acceptance gate. Level 9 weakened earlier layouts.
No extra crates/modules/dependencies, unsafe code, filesystem, environment,
processes or networking. Keep code compact (roughly 150-250 lines), bounds-check
dimensions and checked arithmetic before allocations. Stateless train is fine.
Use binary varints or fixed integers for compact counted transform metadata.

Generic arbitrary bytes, empty input, NUL, malformed CSV, CRLF, final lines
without newline, JSON duplicate keys and numeric spelling variations MUST
round-trip through encode/decode directly. Use a tagged plain zstd fallback for
unsupported layouts. The wrapper's raw escape is not a substitute for a correct
algorithm. Compare alternatives in encode if needed, then record the chosen tag.
Bound inputs at 2 MiB, output/model at the API limits. Exact bytes matter: never
round decimals, discard exceptions, canonicalize quoting or assume learned
equality, timestamps or column counts always hold. Never embed sample records.
The host adds/counts a 40-byte frame plus a common corpus container. Numeric
tokens are often DOUBLE-QUOTED, space-padded, and written with long decimal
fractions or scientific exponents. The statistics unwrap these only for analysis;
your inverse must retain the quotes, padding and spelling, or use a reversible
fallback for unsupported tokens. Detect raw layout conditions before transforming.

use crate::{Codec, CodecError};
use crate::toolkit::{zstd_compress, zstd_decompress};

// Byteplane / position-transpose experiment for quoted numeric CSV lexemes.
// Transform: split raw bytes into lines (LF/CRLF/CR/final-none preserved per
// line) and naive comma columns (quotes/padding/spelling kept byte-exact in
// tokens). Candidate T1 concatenates each column row-major with NUL
// separators; candidate T2 ("byteplanes") groups each column by character
// position p (all p-th bytes across rows) plus exact token lengths, so fixed-
// width decimals / exponents align. Everything is compared against plain zstd
// at level 19 in encode and the smallest wins (tagged fallback). No numeric
// conversion, rounding, or quote normalization ever happens.
// Limitations: only rectangular comma layouts without NUL bytes are
// transformed; JSON, single-column, ragged/malformed CSV, embedded NUL, and
// tiny inputs use the tagged raw-zstd fallback. Quoted commas/newlines are
// treated as delimiters (still exactly invertible via stored dimensions) so
// compression may be poor there but bytes round-trip.

pub struct Candidate;

const TAG_RAW: u8 = 0;
const TAG_COL: u8 = 1;
const TAG_PLANE: u8 = 2;

fn put_varint(out: &mut Vec<u8>, mut v: u64) {
    while v >= 0x80 {
        out.push((v as u8) | 0x80);
        v >>= 7;
    }
    out.push(v as u8);
}

fn get_varint(b: &[u8], mut p: usize) -> Option<(u64, usize)> {
    let mut s = 0u32;
    let mut v = 0u64;
    loop {
        let x = *b.get(p)?;
        p += 1;
        v |= ((x & 0x7f) as u64).checked_shl(s)? as u64;
        s = s.checked_add(7)?;
        if x & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Some((v, p));
        }
        if s > 70 {
            return None;
        }
    }
}

fn raw_fallback(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError> {
    let mut c = zstd_compress(input, 19).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut o = Vec::with_capacity(c.len().checked_add(1).ok_or("len")?);
    o.push(TAG_RAW);
    o.append(&mut c);
    if o.len() > crate::MAX_PAYLOAD {
        return Err("payload".into());
    }
    Ok(o)
}

// Parse lines + rectangular comma grid. Returns (line_contents, endings, ncols).
fn parse_grid(
    input: &[u8],
) -> Option<(Vec<(u32, u32)>, Vec<u8>, usize)> {
    if input.is_empty() || input.contains(&0) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut lines: Vec<(u32, u32)> = Vec::new();
    let mut ends: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut s = 0usize;
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < input.len() {
        if input[i] == b'\r' {
            let e = if i + 1 < input.len() && input[i + 1] == b'\n' {
                i += 2;
                1u8
            } else {
                i += 1;
                2u8
            };
            lines.push((s as u32, (if e == 1 { i - 2 } else { i - 1 }) as u32));
            ends.push(e);
            s = i;
        } else if input[i] == b'\n' {
            lines.push((s as u32, i as u32));
            ends.push(0u8);
            i += 1;
            s = i;
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    if s < input.len() {
        lines.push((s as u32, input.len() as u32));
        ends.push(3u8);
    } else if s == input.len() && (lines.is_empty()) {
        return None;
    }
    if lines.len() < 2 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut ncols: Option<usize> = None;
    for (a, b) in lines.iter() {
        let mut n = 1usize;
        for k in (*a as usize)..(*b as usize) {
            if input[k] == b',' {
                n = n.checked_add(1)?;
            }
        }
        match ncols {
            None => ncols = Some(n),
            Some(c) if c != n => return None,
        }
    }
    let nc = ncols?;
    if nc < 2 || nc > 1024 || lines.len() > 200_000 {
        return None;
    }
    let toks = (lines.len() as u64).checked_mul(nc as u64)?;
    if toks > 4_000_000 {
        return None;
    }
    Some((lines, ends, nc))
}

fn token_spans(
    input: &[u8],
    lines: &[(u32, u32)],
    ncols: usize,
) -> Option<Vec<(u32, u32)>> {
    let n = lines.len().checked_mul(ncols)?;
    let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    for (a, b) in lines.iter() {
        let mut f = *a as usize;
        for _ in 0..ncols {
            let mut e = f;
            while e < (*b as usize) && input[e] != b',' {
                e += 1;
            }
            if e - f > 8192 {
                return None;
            }
            t.push((f as u32, e as u32));
            f = e + 1;
        }
    }
    Some(t)
}

fn build_meta(nrows: usize, ncols: usize, ends: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut m = Vec::with_capacity(32 + ends.len());
    put_varint(&mut m, nrows as u64);
    put_varint(&mut m, ncols as u64);
    m.extend_from_slice(ends);
    m
}

    fn encode(input: &[u8], _model: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError> {

            Some(g) => g,
        };

            Some(t) => t,
        };

        }

        for c in 0..ncols {

                    let (a, b) = toks[r * ncols + c];
                    let len = (b - a) as usize;

                    }

        }

        let (tag, zb) = if z1.len() < z2.len() && z1.len() < raw.len() {

        } else if z2.len() < raw.len() {

            let mut o = Vec::with_capacity(raw.len() + 1);
            o.push(TAG_RAW);
            o.extend_from_slice(&raw);
            if o.len() > crate::MAX_PAYLOAD {

            return Ok(o);
        };

    }

    fn decode(
        encoded: &[u8],

        original_len: usize,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError> {
        if original_len > crate::MAX_INPUT {
